scenario.title: Single departure checkpoint, synthetic day with a congested morning peak

statistics.quantileMethod: linear interpolation between order statistics (Hyndman-Fan type 7)

assumptions.note: All lanes open all day; planned lane schedules arrive in a later slice.
About 90 passengers per hour per lane.
Design day with a morning bank of departures, typical of low-cost bases.
Nominal walking time from the checkpoint exit to the gate zone.
Triangular distribution, drawn per flight and replication.
Connecting passengers who cross this checkpoint. Not an official statistic.
Arrival at the checkpoint = STD minus (25 min + log-normal with median 70 min).
Connecting passengers arrive later, after their inbound flight.
Individual walking time = nominal zone time x log-normal(median 1, sigma).
Boarding closes 20 minutes before the scheduled departure, for every flight.
The system applies the closing rule to the schedule; in this slice it matches the ground truth exactly.

modelLimitations: Single checkpoint with all lanes open all day: no lane schedules, outages or extra lanes.
Calls are answered instantly: no call latency, no no-shows and no recalls.
The system's deadline equals the ground truth (boarding close from a fixed rule): no flight delays, gate changes or stale data.
Passengers never abandon the queue, even after their flight has closed.
No groups, families or assisted passengers: everyone is served individually.
The baseline is pure FIFO. Today's manual handling of urgent passengers is not modelled, so the benefit of prioritisation is likely overstated.
Tickets are issued on arrival with no kiosk or scanning delay.
The engine estimates processing time as the mean screening time and walking time as the nominal time of the gate zone.
